title: Spark Savings v2 separates default admin, setter and taker into distinct addresses per instance
content:
Every Spark Savings v2 instance's `Instance-specific Operational Parameters → Contract Addresses` block lists exactly four entries: `Spark Vault v2 Implementation`, `Default admin`, `Setter`, and `Taker` — see A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.4.1 (Avalanche USDC), .3.5.1.1.4.1 (Robinhood Chain USDG) and .3.6.1.1.4.1 (X Layer USDT).

The addresses differ per instance and differ from each other within an instance, which means the role split is real deployment topology, not documentation convention.

The separation maps onto the two dangerous powers a savings vault holds. The **setter** controls the yield offered to depositors — abuse mints unearned liability. The **taker** controls movement of deposited assets — abuse removes them. Splitting these means no single compromised key can both quietly reprice the vault and drain it, and the **default admin** sits above both as the role-granting authority.

This is what makes the `Unlimited` take rate limit tolerable: the compensating control is not a throttle but key separation. It also means the security of hundreds of millions in deposits reduces to the operational security of three distinct address holders per chain — a burden that grows linearly with each new instance the Artifact registers.
description: Each vault instance publishes four addresses — implementation, default admin, setter, taker — so rate-setting authority and asset-movement authority are held by different keys.
